'''Karl Wolfgang Böer''' (March 23, 1926<ref>[http://socialarchive.iath.virginia.edu/ark:/99166/w6xq0m37 Biographical notes about Böer, K. W. (Karl Wolfgang), 1926] - SNAC</ref> – April 18, 2018)<ref>[http://www.udel.edu/udaily/2018/april/in-memoriam-karl-w-boer/ In Memoriam: Karl W. Böer]</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://m.legacy.com/obituaries/delawareonline/obituary.aspx?n=karl-wolfgang-boer&pid=188806249&referrer=0&preview=false|title=Karl Wolfgang Boer Obituary (1926 - 2018) the News Journal |website=[[Legacy.com]] }}</ref> was a [[solar energy]] pioneer and expert in the field of semiconductor physics.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-04-23 |title=In Memoriam: Karl W. Böer {{!}} UDaily |url=https://www.udel.edu/udaily/2018/april/in-memoriam-karl-w-boer/ |access-date=2023-01-23 |website=www.udel.edu |publisher=[[University of Delaware]] |language=en}}</ref>

==Biography==
Born in [[Berlin, Germany]], he earned a Ph.D. from Humboldt University, Berlin (Diploma, Physics, 1949; Doctorate, Physics and Solid State Physics, 1952, 1955).<ref name="Library Collections Department">{{cite web|title=Karl Wolfgang Boer Papers|url=http://www.lib.udel.edu/ud/spec/findaids/boer/|publisher=University of Delaware|date=1945–2003}}</ref>

Böer founded [[Physica Status Solidi]] and subsequently published its first issue in July 1961.  Physica Status Solidi is a family of international peer-reviewed, scientific journals, publishing research on all aspects of solid state physics, and material science. It is owned and published by [[Wiley-VCH]].<ref>[[Physica Status Solidi]]</ref>  Böer served as editor.

Böer also founded and became the director of the Section of Dielectric Breakdown of the [[German Academy of Sciences at Berlin|German Academy of Science in Berlin]].

With the construction of the [[Berlin Wall]], Böer made a decision to emigrate to the [[United States]]. In 1962, he began as an associate professor the [[University of Delaware]].  He became professor of physics in 1965, professor of physics and engineering in 1972, and distinguished professor of physics and solar energy in 1993 at the University of Delaware.<ref name="Library Collections Department"/>

Böer led the discovery of solar energy technologies by focusing his work on the efficiency of [[Copper(I) sulfide]] and [[cadmium sulfide]] (Cu<sub>2</sub>S/CdS) used in [[thin film]] solar conversions.

In 1973, Böer built an experimental house called the Solar One, the first house to convert sunlight into energy.<ref>{{cite web|last=Kozlowski|first=Lori|title=Solar Power: Karl Wolfgang Boer and a Lifetime of Green Discoveries|url=http://latimesblogs.latimes.com/greenspace/2010/10/solar-power-green-energy-karl-wolfgang-boer-.html|work=Los Angeles Times|date=October 2010|accessdate=1 October 2010}}</ref>

He is credited with writing articles in over 300 publications,<ref>{{cite web|last=Boer|first=Karl Wolfgang|title=Special Collections Department|url=http://www.lib.udel.edu/ud/spec/findaids/boer/app.htm|publisher=University of Delaware|date=1961–1986}}</ref> along with several books.  His latest, released in 2010, is "The Life of the Solar Pioneer.<ref>{{cite book|last=Boer|first=Karl Wolfgang|title=The Life of the Solar Pioneer Karl Wolfgang Boer|year=2013|publisher=iUniverse.com|isbn=978-1450228787|pages=336|url=http://karlwboer.com/|archive-date=2013-09-11|access-date=2013-09-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130911025117/http://karlwboer.com/|url-status=dead}}</ref>   In 2018, he eventually published the Reference Work "Semiconductor Physics“ with [[Udo W. Pohl]].<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Böer |first1=Karl W. |url=https://link.springer.com/referencework/10.1007/978-3-319-69150-3 |title=Semiconductor Physics |last2=Pohl |first2=Udo W. |author-link2=Udo W. Pohl |publisher=Springer International Publishing |year=2018 |isbn=978-3-319-69148-0 |edition=1st |doi=10.1007/978-3-319-69150-3 |bibcode=2018seph.book.....B |language=en}}</ref> Böer also holds 28 patents in the area of solid state technology. His book, Survey of Semiconductor Physics (1993) has been called the most comprehensive treatment in the field written by a single author.

The University of Delaware awards a Karl W. Böer Solar Energy Medal of Merit every two years. The award recognizes those who have made a significant contribution to solar as well as honors Böer for his initial contributions to the [[Solar power in the United States|solar industry]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2001 Karl W. Boer Solar Energy Medal of Merit|url=http://www.solarnovus.com/2011-karl-w-boer-solar-energy-medal-of-merit_N2866.html|publisher=Solar Novus}}</ref>

==Awards==

* 1965 American Physical Society, Fellow
* 1998 Medal of Distinction, University of Delaware
* 2000 American Solar Energy Society, Fellow
* 2001 Institute of Electric and Electronic Engineers
* 2012 American Solar Energy Society Lifetime Leadership Award<ref>{{cite web|title=ASES Lifetime Leadership Award|url=http://www.ases.org/ases-lifetime-leadership-award/|publisher=ASES}}</ref>
